notes: Editing a trigger changes the draft revision only. The current active schedule is shown separately until validation and activation.
Time, timezone, days and missed-run policy are explicit. Daylight-saving transitions resolve using the selected timezone.
Saving the trigger never activates the automation or performs its downstream external actions.

title: Connect · Compose a message
source: Owner revision 28 October; UX27-OTHER-003–004; Mail identity, draft and send boundaries
notes: From identity, recipients, subject, attachments and retained draft status are visible in the same compose surface.
Adding recipients resolves the selected contact explicitly; drafting does not send or grant tool access.
The send menu opens scheduling as a separate review. Attachment upload status is visible before sending.

title: Connect · Schedule send review
source: Owner revision 28 October; Mail scheduled send and durable outbox semantics
notes: A scheduled message retains the original draft, actual sender, recipients, selected timezone and attachment state.
Scheduling is distinct from provider submission and sent confirmation. The user can edit or cancel before dispatch.
A failure at dispatch leaves the message recoverable with a visible outbox error.

title: Maps · Route options and stops
source: Owner revision 28 October; Maps canonical routes, mode and source metadata
notes: The options panel edits the same route, including travel mode, stops and preferences.
Estimated route data retains its map/provider source and freshness; this fixture is illustrative rather than navigation guidance.
A failed or unavailable route remains visibly unresolved instead of substituting a generated route.

title: Shelf · Add an item
source: Owner revision 28 October; Shelf canonical LaunchItems and collection references
notes: A Shelf item references the original app, document, website or platform target. It does not move or duplicate the original.
The picker shows the target identity and destination collection before adding it.
Unavailable targets can remain as recoverable entries and must not silently resolve to another item.

title: Vision & Voice · Sources and capture
source: Owner revision 28 October; UX27-SPACES-014; explicit capture and retention
notes: The source sheet separates camera, screen, microphone and retained transcript permissions.
A source must be explicitly selected before it becomes live context. Disabled capture is never inferred from an active microphone.
Stopping capture removes that live source; transcript retention remains a separate choice.

title: Build · Code workspace
source: UX27-BUILD-001–007; Dev: Editor and navigation, Visual CUI Builder, AI ChangeSet model
notes: Dev, Sites and Stacks remain domains of one Build project. Switching surfaces retains the project and revision.
Preview identifies its source and environment; a failed build must label the last valid preview as stale.
The explorer, editor, tests and typed AI changes address canonical files. Review AI edits as a diff before applying them.
Code and diagnostics use monospace. Ordinary chrome inherits the shared CUI theme.

title: Build · Sites editor
source: UX27-BUILD-001,004,006; Sites: Visual Page Editor, Responsive design, Preview fidelity, Deployment safeguards
notes: Sites editing and Code operate on the same project, components and source revision.
The public page appears inside an isolated preview. Its fonts, colours and styles never become editor chrome.
Responsive preview and selected-component properties represent the same source model.
Preview, staging and production are separate states. Publish must show its environment and changes before committing.

title: Build · Stacks conflict review
source: UX27-BUILD-005; Stacks: Branch/Twig/Leaf, active domain, conflicts, Roots and Freeze
notes: Branch, Twig and Leaf are nested development domains. Their active selection must be explicit.
Review identifies base, local and incoming revisions and the exact conflicting file.
Accept without Merging, Accept and Merge and Reject are distinct operations. Reject preserves the original work.
Root and Freeze restrictions remain enforceable outside the UI. Commit, push, merge and deployment are different states.

title: AI Studio · Agent builder and test
source: AI Studio: navigation, Agent Builder, advanced logic, Playground; UX27-OTHER-013
notes: The Agent resolves its stable Den identity. Editing configuration does not create a replacement Agent.
Model, tools, instructions, knowledge and permissions are typed definitions, shared between form and graph views.
Testing runs the draft under an explicit profile. Test success does not activate or install it.
Build, Test & Debug and Resources expose distinct destinations. The consumer conversation remains in Spaces.

title: Terminal · Command workspace
source: Terminal: AI / Command mode switcher, PTY sessions, tabs and panes; UX27-OTHER-012
notes: Command mode executes in the visible selected shell. AI mode is a separate input route; ordinary commands are not sent to a model.
Every pane shows its actual session, working directory and process state. Switching panes must not silently retarget pending input.
A disconnected remote session retains its transcript and explains reconnect semantics.
Closing a tab must make its effect on the owned process clear. Text selection is distinct from command input.

title: Mini Computer · Virtual machine
source: Mini Computer: viewer, lifecycle, snapshots, clipboard trust; UX27-OTHER-017
notes: The viewer identifies the machine, provider, connection and input owner. View-only and control are distinct.
Closing the viewer leaves the VM running. Pause, save state, stop and shutdown are explicit lifecycle operations.
Clipboard, folders and device sharing have visible independent permissions.
Snapshots and runtime changes retain canonical VM identity; reconnect never invents a replacement session.

title: Games · Scene and components
source: Games: CUI-native editor, scene graph, purposeful components; UX27-OTHER-015
notes: Scene hierarchy, viewport, components and assets select the same stable object identity.
Development and Creation/Rendering share one project. Play/test is explicit and does not overwrite authored scene state.
The CUI Visual Builder owns game UI authoring; gameplay, material and animation graphs use appropriate registered nodes.
The persistent AI bar receives semantic scene/project context rather than falling back to generic computer use.

title: Link · Continuous Flow document
source: TF-L01–02: Link shell and Flow; TF-X01
notes: Flow combines inline content in one primary vertical scroll. Do not turn sources into independent scrolling panels or file cards.
The mandatory report composition can include Data, Write, an image, another section of the same Data source and a scoped report assistant.
References retain source identity and visible live/pinned policies. Edit original and authored Flow edits are different actions.
Returning from an original editor restores the reader to the same Flow position. Source permission is checked independently of Flow access.

title: Link · Binder overview and detail
source: TF-L01, TF-L03: Binder overview, authored containers and nonlinear navigation
notes: Binder is one authored interconnected document. Its notes, folders, tabs and stacks contain real nested content.
File references preserve their originals. Rearranging a Binder never moves the source file.
Reader mode retains nonlinear open/close, breadcrumbs, Back and outline while hiding layout handles.
Opening and closing a container restores the surrounding viewport and focus. Source editing requires separate source permission.

title: Prototype · Interactive spring explorer
source: TF-P01–03: typed model, Design / Logic / Run and session-local inputs
notes: Prototype models interactive systems, calculations and simulations; it is not limited to UI or 3D mock-ups.
Design, Logic and Run operate on one typed model with stable object/property IDs.
Runtime input changes are session-local. Applying them as saved defaults is a separate author action.
Formulas, units, assumptions and derived outputs remain inspectable. Invalid dependencies must show errors rather than plausible invented values.

title: Paths · Branching learning route
source: TF-H01–03: step outline, route graph, preview and durable reader progress
notes: Path authoring combines the step outline, route graph, content and conditions over stable step IDs.
Each choice names its destination. Conditions, fallback routes and invalid routes remain inspectable.
Preview has disposable test progress and identifies its draft revision; it never changes a reader attempt.
Reader progress is durable and separate from authoring. A branching path must not invent a fixed completion percentage.

title: Replay · Historical checkpoint
source: TF-R01–03: semantic capture, historical viewer, timeline and sharing review
notes: Replay records selected semantic revisions, events and checkpoints. Optional media is supplementary.
The historical viewer identifies the captured revision and stays read-only even when the source has advanced.
Missing intervals and dependencies remain visible as incomplete capture, never invented reconstruction.
Continue from here makes an independent copy through the owning app. It must never overwrite the current original.

title: Present · Compare Variants
source: TF-V01–03: integrated Variants; Present canonical slide/object comparison
notes: Variants is integrated into Present, not a separate app. The active branch appears beside document identity.
Compare names the source, base and target; additions, edits and conflicts use more than colour alone.
Selected changes are previewed before a semantic merge against explicit revisions. A stale preview must be refreshed.
Switching or merging variants preserves both branches and does not publish or present the artifact.

title: 9to1 Admin · People and policy scope
source: ADM-01–12: organisation identity, people, roles, policies and deployment state
notes: Every administrative screen displays the current organisation. Product entitlement does not confer admin privileges.
People states distinguish invited, active, suspended and removed. Effective permissions include role, policy and object scope.
Policy changes move through Draft, Validated and Published, then show per-target enforcement. An offline endpoint is not silently compliant.
Bulk changes preview their scope and report per-item outcomes. Personal accounts and unrelated organisations remain separate.

title: 9to1OS · Desktop and Go
source: 9to1-OS: desktop shell, Taskbar Layers, Desktop Spaces, Quick Settings; Go: search and typed actions
notes: The default shell uses conventional window controls and a taskbar with Go at the start.
Taskbar Layers are discrete, with one to five layers and a visible position indicator. They are separate from virtual desktops and Desktop Spaces.
Go is a shared Search / AI and typed-action surface. Results retain canonical source and permission checks.
Go is the active shell popup; opening Quick Settings dismisses unrelated transient surfaces. This mock-up is intended layout, not OS implementation evidence.

title: Launcher · Mobile home
source: Launcher: home pages, app drawer, dock, widgets and extreme customisation
notes: Launcher owns Android-style home pages, folders, widgets, app drawer and dock. It is distinct from Shelf and Home package management.
Grid, icon size, dock, folders, gestures and wallpaper are configurable while retaining canonical app identities.
Touch targets remain usable. Widgets use their owning app data and declared permissions.
Search / Go and Dulche are first-class entry points. The screen shows a saved home layout, not a fixed product-wide arrangement.

title: Build · Completion and diagnostics
source: UX27-BUILD-002–004; Dev / Language intelligence, diagnostics and Visual CUI Builder; CUI / Hot reload and error boundaries
notes: Completion, signature information, diagnostics and quick fixes resolve semantic symbols in the current source revision. Accepting completion is one undoable text edit.
The invalid in-progress member name produces a navigable diagnostic at the actual file and line. The preview retains the last valid tree and is labelled Last valid.
Draft text is preserved on validation failure. The current preview is not evidence that an invalid draft built successfully.
Keyboard acceptance, dismissal and focus return belong to the editor; navigation to a diagnostic preserves the current file identity and selection.

title: Build Sites · Mobile breakpoint
source: UX27-BUILD-004,006; Sites / Responsive design, Visual Page Editor and Preview fidelity
notes: The mobile preview is the same canonical Home page and Hero component at a 390px viewport; it is not a copied mobile page.
Inspector controls distinguish inherited Desktop values from explicit Mobile overrides, with reset-to-inherited actions and clear breakpoint scope.
Responsive properties update the supported site model and remain undoable. Visual preview and authored breakpoint rules must stay consistent.
Changing a breakpoint or preview width never publishes the site. Production deployment remains a separate reviewed action.

title: Build Stacks · Freeze scope
source: Stacks / Roots, Freeze and Freeze lifecycle and permissions; UX27-BUILD-005
notes: Freeze marks a specific resource or domain out of scope for a selected descendant scope. Root authority and Freeze state are separate concepts.
The details view identifies the frozen target, scope, creator, reason, creation revision, optional expiry condition and affected descendants.
Editing or thawing a Freeze requires the configured management permission. Descendant editing or an AI instruction cannot bypass an active Freeze.
Expiry or thaw rechecks in-progress work and reconciles queued upstream changes. A thaw request does not silently apply those changes or report completion.

title: AI Studio · Agent tool permissions
source: AI Studio / Agent Builder and Tool Builder; UX27-OTHER-013; Home / Permission and trust broker
notes: Tool policy is part of the versioned Agent draft and uses the same definition as its graph. Draft, active revision and test profile remain distinct.
The selected source scope and action policy are explicit. A source-reading grant does not authorise Forms creation or access to unrelated private sources.
Simulation and a successful test cannot grant live permission. Activating a definition remains separate from account-level authorisation.
Every protected action is checked by its owning app and Home broker. Mandatory action approvals cannot be disabled by this builder.

title: Terminal · Review an AI command
source: Terminal / AI and Command modes, approval and PTY sessions; UX27-OTHER-012
notes: The proposed command is shown before execution with the actual shell, session, working directory and privilege context. This example is configured to review AI-generated commands.
Command and AI modes remain visible and distinct. Copying a suggestion to the command field does not execute it; Run once is an explicit separate action.
The transcript is previous terminal output. The new command is clearly Not executed and has no fabricated exit code or result.
The terminal adapter receives the approved command for the selected session only. Closing the review leaves unrelated processes and the other pane running.

title: Link Binder · Add content
notes: Binder’s palette adds real authored notes, cards, folders, tabbed binders, stacks, sections, connections and shared content objects.
The destination is the selected Research container, identified independently from its title. Adding a source creates a reference without moving or duplicating the original file.
Directly authored content stays within Binder. Referenced source editing is separately permissioned and uses the owning app.
Insert, remove, reorder and nested navigation preserve stable container/item identities. Closing the palette restores the same overview and focus.

title: Link Flow · Source section and placement
notes: The selected Flow block retains a canonical source and stable section identity. Live or pinned revision policy is explicit and separate from arrangement.
Move, duplicate placement and remove operate on the Flow sequence without copying or deleting the source file.
Flow layout permission and source-edit permission are independent. This state permits arranging the block but presents the source as view-only.
Continuous reading and one primary scroll remain intact. A source editor opens through its own registered capability and returns to the same Flow position.

title: Prototype · Edit a typed input
notes: The selected slider binds to the stable typed mass property. Name, type, units, default, limits and step are editable model data rather than an isolated visual control.
The proposed default 2.5 kg is pending; the current preview still uses its existing 2.0 kg input. Applying defaults is a separate authoring action.
Validation enforces constraints and previews dependent outputs. Renaming or adjusting a property must preserve bindings and undo history.
Session-local Run inputs remain separate from saved defaults; Reset uses the declared initial state and cannot repeat external effects.

title: Paths · Edit a route condition
notes: Each choice has a stable target, human-readable label, explicit condition and defined missing-value behaviour. Graph position does not identify a route.
This draft condition reads the authored Welcome confidence response. Required type, comparison and threshold are visible, with an always-available alternative route.
Preview uses disposable test inputs bound to the draft revision. It must not change real reader progress or publish a new authored revision.
A false condition does not randomly choose another route. Missing values produce the configured recoverable state; validation detects missing targets, unreachable outcomes and uncontrolled loops.

title: Replay · Inspect a recorded change
notes: The event identifies the captured source, actor, timestamp and historical revision. The rendered checkpoint is read-only and separate from the current source.
Before/after content belongs to the recorded semantic event and source revision. Seeking or playback reconstructs history; it does not execute the original mutation again.
Sharing review can exclude or redact captured material without deleting the current original. Access and capture completeness remain explicit.
Continue from here requests an independent copy through the owning app, preserving the source. Open current file uses the current source’s actual permissions.

title: Files · Sheet and organisation types
source: TF-F01–TF-F11; TF-F04 (Sheet); UX27-FILES-001–004
notes: Files owns Folder, Project, Sheet, Tree, Smart, Timeline, Pipeline, Catalogue, Stash and Matrix. The New menu exposes all ten; each keeps the standard Files shell and compatible nesting.
Every specialised organisation offers an ordinary Contents view without erasing coordinates, sections, membership or metadata. Tree additionally requires editor rights for its visual Tree view.
A Sheet arranges references, notes, drawings and shapes. Add existing defaults to Add reference; removing an appearance does not delete or move its original.

The Sheet default File opening setting is Pop-up. In authoring, click selects and the explicit Open action opens; a safe owning editor must disclose that it edits the original. Source permissions remain independent.
Selection, viewport and view choice belong to the current user. Authored geometry, connector endpoints, shared layout and opening policy persist as Sheet state.

title: Spaces · Experiences
source: Spaces / First-party Spaces / Experiences (canonical experience state, checkpoints and branching); UX27-SPACES-001–014; UX27-OTHER-016; PPT slides 8–15 (conversation shell)
notes: The normal Space conversation remains the primary interaction surface. Inventory, evidence and scene panels represent canonical Experience state rather than a separate hidden game runtime.
Narrated state changes become usable only after the corresponding structured transition commits. The evidence-added event and State revision 18 indicate the same committed transition.
Checkpoint branching preserves both conversation history and matching Experience-state revision; the original timeline remains intact. Rewind cannot undo already completed external actions.
Visible state follows the experience and character visibility policy. Private clues, unknown character knowledge and hidden outcomes must not leak through side panels or generated UI.

Experiences supports open-ended stories, roleplay, simulations and mysteries. Formal contestant, round and scoring state belongs to Play; age-appropriate controls and normal Space permissions remain in force.
The shared Spaces composer uses the separate conversation-permissions switch and rounded icon-only action stack. It retains the same draft and current experience context.

title: Appearance · Theme and accent preferences
source: CUI-PREF-201–205; CUI-THEME-001–004; UX27-SHARED-005; authoritative PPT 1–6
notes: Current picker contains eight built-ins plus Create Theme. Cinematic is handled as a legacy preference, never silently relabelled.
Authenticated settings are account-wide through Home. Device cache supports offline use without becoming a competing authority.
Accent modes are None, All Apps and Individual Apps. None retains each app’s specified accent; per-app choices still belong to Home settings.

Bubble uses watery dimensional controls and an optional click wobble; Western uses an original wood texture with sepia limited to chrome icons; Retro uses terminal-style monochrome panels, monospace chrome and restrained effects. These follow the latest owner refinement. Frosted Glass has no Gaussian/Mica; that material remains reserved for Professional.

Theme changes preserve active document, selection, scroll position, topology and authored colours. Reduced Motion removes Bubble wobble and Retro active effects; no content or action depends on an animation.

title: Create Theme · Authoring and preview
source: CUI-PREF-204–205; CUI-PRO-203; CUI inherited themes and typed fallback
notes: Primary, Secondary and Tertiary each independently choose Solid Colour, Gradient or Pattern, with authored transparency and supported blur.
All seven font roles expose family, weight and size. Button Roundness accepts the full 0–100% range.
This custom theme inherits Professional, so supported backdrop blur can be authored. Preview does not modify the saved preference until Save.
An app override recolours only Primary, preserving gradient stops, pattern geometry, transparency and blur; Secondary/Tertiary remain authored.
Hover Effects and Custom Cursors are later enhancements and are not presented as enabled controls.

title: Components · Buttons, inputs and control states
source: Authoritative PPT slides 1–6; UX27-SHARED-002–008/019; CUI-THEME-004
notes: Primary, Secondary, Tertiary, Negative and Text buttons retain their semantic hierarchy in Professional and Glow. Accent-dependent colours resolve through the selected theme.
Hover morphs, pressed feedback and focus are distinct. The slide’s bounce becomes a restrained interruptible press response; reduced motion removes movement.
Five-second destructive hold is one optional pointer path. A keyboard/single-activation review dialog provides an equally explicit accessible confirmation route.
Input focus, invalid and disabled states remain distinct. Active controls never inherit disabled parent opacity.
Shared Feedback/Reveal/Reflow/Panel durations are 100/140/180/220 ms draft defaults; input, caret, save truth and permissions do not wait for animation.

Professional/Glow component examples preserve the deck’s blue/orange palette. Dark labels on bright Glow/red hover fills retain contrast. The six other themes are new design definitions; Professional material always has an opaque fallback.

title: States · Recovery and persistence reference
source: UX27-SHARED-014–019; UX27-BOARD-003–009; TF-02; Files sync/availability rules
notes: Loading, empty, failure, offline, denied and conflict each have distinct copy, icon and meaningful next action.
Local durability and cloud sync are independent. A pending upload never erases a Saved locally state.
Recovery retains the existing document and unsaved draft. Retry reconciles the same operation when duplicate effects are possible.
Permission denial never invents content or switches to another account automatically. Conflict review preserves both versions until resolved.

title: Bubble · Material and controls
source: Owner theme refinement, 28 October 2026; CUI-PREF-201–205; CUI-THEME-001–004; Retro category reference: https://opencode.ai/docs/themes/
notes: Water-like highlights and refracted edge light give controls depth. Gloss is restricted to control surfaces; text retains stable contrast and authored paper colours stay unchanged.
A click applies one 520 ms damped wobble to the activated control. State and action feedback occur immediately; animation never delays execution, save or permission changes.
Reduced Motion and the operating-system preference both remove movement. There is no ambient loop, floating layout or full-screen blur.
Light mode uses pale water surfaces and dark teal text. High contrast omits material decoration; focus and selected states remain separately visible.
The sample document is authored content: its cream paper, type and ink remain identical under every theme. Theme selection does not edit the document or grant any tool permission.

title: Western · Material and controls
source: Owner theme refinement, 28 October 2026; CUI-PREF-201–205; CUI-THEME-001–004; Retro category reference: https://opencode.ai/docs/themes/
notes: The build embeds one original photographic wood texture in --western-wood-image. Host, address and selected chrome use that same asset at preserved aspect ratio with strong readability overlays.
Sepia applies to chrome icons only. App symbols remain recognisable; source images, authored slide/document content, graphs, ink and Assistant portraits are never filtered.
Dark mode uses an inlaid dark address bar; light mode uses a pale waxed-wood treatment. Subtle inset edges and grain create material detail without obscuring labels.
No layout, toolbar tier, control location or navigation topology changes. Reduced Motion remains honoured; wood and the slight vignette are static.
The sample document is authored content: its cream paper, type and ink remain identical under every theme. Theme selection does not edit the document or grant any tool permission.

title: Retro · Material and controls
source: Owner theme refinement, 28 October 2026; CUI-PREF-201–205; CUI-THEME-001–004; Retro category reference: https://opencode.ai/docs/themes/
notes: Modern terminal conventions inform the charcoal panels, monochrome hierarchy, monospace chrome, sharp control cells and hard offset shadows. OpenCode’s public theme documentation is a category reference, not a product or branding copy.
Static scanlines and dither are limited to chrome at low opacity. They do not cover document pixels, charts, authored colour, video frames, images or ink.
The optional 160 ms active response is a single small text-shadow displacement, without flashing content. Reduced Motion removes it; there is no continuous scan animation.
App accents and semantic status colours remain distinct. Light mode uses a legible paper-terminal palette; themes retain the same toolbar/container geometry.
The sample document is authored content: its cream paper, type and ink remain identical under every theme. Theme selection does not edit the document or grant any tool permission.

title: Settings · Account & subscription
source: Home / Settings and Account and subscription surface; Accounts & Subscription / Profile customisation — required and optional fields; Canonical subscription state; Custom resource allocation
notes: Name and Username are the only required profile fields; Icon, Pronouns and Job are optional and clearable. Profile changes preserve CAKE ID, ownership, permissions and entitlements.
The illustrated custom Balanced configuration uses the specification’s £10 allocation example: 35,000 AI Dust and 250 GB. A tier label does not compute entitlements or resource balances.
Dust, storage, prices, entitlement thresholds and sessions come from the authoritative account service. Missing site-limit data remains unavailable rather than a fabricated allocation.
Manage plan, checkout and sensitive billing changes open the trusted authenticated CAKEMODS flow. Session revocation or sign-out does not silently delete local artifacts.

title: Settings · AI & models
source: Home / Discover; Universal Model Picker / Compact picker and full manager, Ordered Model Routes, Local model lifecycle; Dulche Den / Persistent Memory and Memory Frequency; Background Learning
notes: Discovery, routes and local management share the canonical Dulche model catalogue. Chat, Image and Voice are primary categories; Advanced includes Audio and Video. Discovery links retain provider identity and unknown capability metadata.

Active and Background routes are distinct. Candidate ordering is considered only after capability, privacy, availability, entitlement and policy filtering; adding a cloud fallback does not authorise remote disclosure.
Memory Frequency has exactly Never, Sometimes, Often and Always. It affects future autonomous memory creation and does not delete existing memories; Temporary Chats cannot write memories.
Background Learning is separately opt-in and does not substitute for Persistent Memory or grant cloud access. Local runtime, residency and resource settings remain device scoped.
Providers and MCP servers expose authentication, capability, permission and health state; a missing or untested connection is never shown as ready.

title: Settings · Permissions & trust
source: Home / Permission and trust broker; App APIs and automation permissions; UX27-SHARED-001; platform shared AI-bar access-mode contract; current owner revision (Spaces Conversation permissions)
notes: Show stable caller identity/origin, target apps/actions/scopes, trust level, creation, expiry and last use. Trust can be temporary, 30-day or always, but never bypasses a target’s protected action rules.
Narrow, revoke, block and unblock operate through the Home broker. Revocation governs future protected actions, with truthful handling of any operation already in flight.
Spaces exposes Conversation permissions as a scoped control for the current conversation. It cannot broaden the account’s grants or the current Space’s policy.
Conversation permissions are separate from an editor’s AI Read-only/Write access mode and from document Edit/Suggest/View. Data still requires explicit approval for every AI mutation.
A changed caller identity or signing/content identity requires re-evaluation; an old friendly name does not silently retain trust.

title: Settings · Apps & updates
source: Home / Apps surface and package management; UX27-HOST-001, UX27-HOST-009; Home / Service registry and compatibility handshake
notes: Home Apps, Settings and Launcher consume the same package/update service and database. Installed, available, dependency, compatibility and repair states retain stable package identity.
Install and update use staged signature/integrity checks, dependency resolution and compatible atomic activation. A failed activation preserves the last validated package when rollback is available.
Download, review and activation are distinct states. Controls show the actual package/version/channel and do not claim an update has completed merely because it was requested.
Uninstall does not delete user-created documents. Artifact retention or deletion is a separate, explicitly scoped operation.

title: Settings · Storage
source: Home / Settings; Accounts & Subscription / Storage usage and Custom resource allocation; Dulche Den / Storage structure and portability; LE-07 / Chat storage, transfer and privacy contract
notes: Local disk usage and account storage are separate measurements and authorities. Installed model files, caches and original documents are distinct categories; model RAM/VRAM is not disk storage.
Conversation placement Local, Mesh and Cloud is separate from AI/tool execution locality. A new chat defaults to Local unless an eligible alternative was explicitly chosen.
Moving managed data or changing placement requires an explicit destination and capability checks. Preview affected items; pending replica cleanup must remain visibly pending.
Caches and search indexes are rebuildable. Cleanup must not remove the only canonical document, Den record, source file or unreadable offline replica.
Account storage allocation shown here is the specification’s custom Balanced example; usage is illustrative account data. Device paths remain device-local.

title: Settings · Mesh & devices
source: Home / Mesh; UX27-OTHER-017; Accounts & Subscription / organisation Mesh; Dulche Den / Synchronisation and conflicts
notes: Mesh is a Home feature. Devices use stable authenticated DeviceIDs and explicit pairing; friendly names do not establish identity or authority.
Sharing is scoped by namespace and selected objects. Pairing does not expose every file, secret, conversation or Assistant; personal and organisation namespaces remain distinct.
Remote invocation uses advertised typed capabilities and both caller and target permissions. Mesh is not implicit remote desktop, input control or arbitrary execution.
Offline devices show queued/unavailable state. Revocation blocks future authentication, sync and remote calls without claiming to erase offline replicas or undo completed actions.
Conflicting revisions are preserved for review; reconnecting does not replay historical requests or completed external effects.

title: Settings · Privacy
source: Privacy and data-protection baseline / Privacy Ceiling; Home / Universal Model Picker / Fallback privacy and control; Dulche Den / DEN-PRIV-001–008; LE-07 / Chat storage, transfer and privacy contract
notes: Show storage locality separately from AI/tool execution. Local conversation storage does not itself authorise or forbid a separately permissioned remote model request.
A configured cloud provider or fallback is not consent to transmit private content. Provider, purpose, context categories and permitted route remain inspectable.

Optional telemetry, diagnostics, personalisation and disclosure have explicit controls with privacy-protective defaults. Credentials and recovery material use secure storage; diagnostic exports redact sensitive content.
Export, deletion and consent withdrawal have visible scope and lifecycle. Replica/index/cache cleanup is reported truthfully rather than merely hiding the primary record.
Persistent Memory, Background Learning and permission to disclose their contents are independent controls; temporary-chat memory write suppression cannot be bypassed.

title: Settings · Accessibility
source: CUI / Accessibility, focus and keyboard semantics; UX27-SHARED-006–008, UX27-SHARED-019; CUI-PRO-201–204; CUI-PREF-202
notes: Reduced motion, high contrast, scale/zoom and non-colour-only states are framework capabilities shared across compatible apps. Theme changes preserve these preferences.
Reduced motion replaces unnecessary movement and preserves truthful progress. Focus remains visible through popovers, tool use and theme changes.
Semantic labels, focus order and keyboard operation follow the shared CUI accessibility tree; inactive controls do not remain hidden keyboard targets.
The preview demonstrates scale, focus and redundant status communication without changing saved document font sizes or authored content.
Account-level accessibility preferences and device input/display adjustments keep explicit scopes; unsupported host facilities must remain unavailable with a reason.

title: Settings · Notifications
source: Home / Notifications; Home / Events typed activity contract (owned by Notifications under current owner revision); UX27-SHARED-001, UX27-SHARED-019
notes: Notifications owns the notification centre, history and typed ecosystem activity; the superseded separate Events destination is not shown.
Each notification/activity item retains stable identity, timestamp, source, category, related entity and typed deep link. Generated digests cannot replace or invent the underlying record.
Read/unread, dismiss, clear and retention policies operate on canonical records. Desktop delivery is a bridge and does not create a competing notification database.
Source/category preferences, previews and delivery channels remain separate controls. A notification action cannot bypass target-app permissions or approval requirements.
Quiet-hours and source controls display effective policy, including any managed restrictions; they cannot silently suppress required security or approval state.

title: Settings · Advanced
source: Home / Service registry and compatibility handshake; Startup, background lifecycle and recovery; Dulche runtime control; 9to1OS / System Log and crash diagnostics; UX27-HOST-009; Privacy baseline
notes: Shared Home Core services expose real version, compatibility and health states. Required service failure gets a scoped repair path; apps preserve their documents instead of launching competing private services.
Dulche lifecycle states include Starting, Ready, Degraded, Restarting and Stopped. Closing the visible Home window does not implicitly terminate dependent background work.

Diagnostics identify component, severity and request/session correlation where available, while redacting secrets and unnecessary personal content. Export is a reviewed local operation; upload is separate.
Rebuildable indexes/caches may be repaired without discarding canonical files, grants, package identities or Den state. Recovery never silently resets durable settings to regain startup.
OS-specific resource reclamation and system-log capabilities must be advertised by the actual host. Desktop UI must not pretend unsupported privileged OS controls are available.

title: Settings · Provider access detail
source: Home / Universal Model Picker / Provider support, Fallback privacy and control; Privacy and data-protection baseline; Dulche MCP / connection, authentication and permission contracts
notes: A provider draft has no verified connectivity, model catalogue or capability state. Test and model discovery use the configured provider adapter and show truthful results.
Authentication references secure credential storage; UI, logs and exports never expose raw tokens. Endpoint and provider identity are distinct from a friendly connection name.
Provider availability and permission to disclose context are separate decisions. Optional memory, learning and background-use grants remain off until explicitly authorised.
Only authorised routes may invoke a provider. Unavailable or denied providers are filtered before route ordering; connection success alone cannot override privacy policy.

title: Mobile · Spaces conversation
source: PPT slides 10–14 adapted to narrow viewport; UX27-SPACES-001–006, 010; UX27-SHARED-003, 010

title: Mobile · Boards page drawer
source: UX27-BOARD-001–047 topology and nested pages; UX27-SHARED-005, 009–010; UX27-TEST-011–014, 033
notes: The narrow layout collapses the nested page sidebar into a named drawer while preserving sections, hierarchy and stable page identities.

title: Mobile · Conversation permissions
source: Owner revision: Spaces permissions icon; Home App API permissions; UX27-SPACES-005–007; UX27-SHARED-010
notes: The separate switch-style composer icon opens a bottom sheet on narrow screens. Spaces has no Read-only/Write segmented control; editor AI modes are unaffected.
The sheet exposes per-tool effective scope and only narrows inherited account grants. Blocked external-send and private-memory access cannot be silently enabled by a conversation override.
Changes still require exact action approval before execution. Save applies conversation preferences to future requests; it is separate from granting a lasting caller trust level.
Touch controls and selects have at least 44-pixel targets. The body scrolls independently while Close, Cancel and Save remain reachable; safe-area padding applies at the bottom.
Dismiss restores the same draft, context and focus. This phone state and the desktop drawer represent the same permission model.

notes: Home is an independent entry point to persistent Assistants. Editors and Spaces reuse the same canonical Assistant identity, portrait, configuration and permanent Main thread.

This current owner decision supersedes any older statement that access must be confined to an Assistants Space; the existing Space conversations remain valid entry points.

title: Home · Specialists
source: Owner revision 28 October: Assistants and Specialists are global identities available from Home and every editor; later steering supersedes Space-only placement; canonical identity, document ownership, Task/Run and permission contracts

title: Present · Working with collaborators
source: Owner revision 28 October: Assistants and Specialists are global identities available from Home and every editor; later steering supersedes Space-only placement; canonical identity, document ownership, Task/Run and permission contracts
notes: Assistant and Specialist avatars join the document header as actual collaborators, with the same stable identities shown in Home and Spaces. Presence is session UI, not authored document content.
The work panel attributes each active task, target and proposed change to its participant. Working, paused, stopped, review-ready and committed states remain distinct.
The owning app keeps the canonical document, object/range identities, revision history and undo. Collaboration does not copy the document into a private Spaces artifact.
Suggest edits is the granted scope here. Write in the contextual AI bar does not waive range limits, current ACLs or review; a proposal remains unapplied until the user accepts the exact change.

Remote selections, transient previews and presence overlays do not enter exports. Revision conflicts require revalidation of the exact change and cannot be resolved by unconditional last-writer-wins.

title: Present · Review an AI change
source: Owner revision 28 October: Assistants and Specialists are global identities available from Home and every editor; later steering supersedes Space-only placement; canonical identity, document ownership, Task/Run and permission contracts
notes: The proposal identifies its author, exact slide/object range, current value and proposed value. Opening review does not apply or authorise it.
Apply this change commits only the displayed operation to the owning document after revision/scope validation, as one undoable transaction.
Keep original rejects this proposal without stopping unrelated authorised work or discarding the participant’s durable task record.
Formatting and surrounding content remain unchanged unless the reviewed operation explicitly includes them. A conflict must refresh the proposal instead of silently overwriting another collaborator.
The local prototype can demonstrate the accepted visual state; it does not claim to implement live provider execution, shared persistence or document-engine acceptance.
